title: BSW.DevSpark Repo Config
description: Repository facts and team policy in .devspark.work/devspark.json. See templates/preamble/configuration.md section 7. This schema is separate from the multi-app registry at .devspark.work/devspark.registry.json.

platform.description: Authoritative git host. Config wins over auto-detection.

organization.description: Azure DevOps organization name (used when platform is azdo).

project.description: Azure DevOps project name (used when platform is azdo).

repository.description: Azure DevOps repository name (used when platform is azdo).

protect_main.description: Team policy: when true, never commit or push directly to the default branch; branch first.

work_tracking.description: Optional Azure DevOps Boards settings. Presence of this block activates work-item commands; absence keeps them entirely inert. Organization and project are read from the top-level fields and must not be repeated here.

default_area_path.description: Area path used when creating items and compared when reviewing them.

default_iteration_path.description: Iteration path applied on creation when it exists for the selected area.

default_work_item_type.description: Type proposed for new items. Always confirmed with the developer, never applied silently.

tags.description: Tags applied to created items in addition to the agent-generated marker tag.

review_on_specify.description: When false, /devspark.specify never offers a work-item review.

pr_risk.description: Optional PR risk digest settings. Absent by default.

tier_patterns.description: Extra case-insensitive regexes matched against changed paths before the built-in table; keys are P0, P1, P2, P3. Tiers are a floor: reviewers may escalate, never lower.

knowledge_drift.description: Optional content-claim drift detection settings. Absent entirely by default; presence never changes legacy stale_entities/--fail-on-stale behavior.

enforcement.description: Sole enforcement opt-in. Only the exact value 'pinned-claims' enables pinned-unverified/drift semantics. Any other present value (including a typo or non-string) is a hard runtime configuration error (exit 2, zero findings) -- the generator never treats a malformed value as opt-out. Absent key keeps legacy behavior indefinitely.
